title: Try another rung only when nothing was sent; after a send, keep the custody the session already has
problem: A fallback that fires when the first route shows no effect cannot tell a silent no-op from an effect that lands late, so it can act twice.
mechanism: Each action returns a delivery outcome (not sent, sent, unknown) and an effect outcome (confirmed, absent at a declared bound, unreadable). Another rung may be tried automatically only when nothing was sent. After a send, an effect absent at the bound is an unknown outcome and no second dispatch follows. What an unknown outcome then does is set by the session's existing custody rule, not by this one. Footwork has three. An ordinary session blocks no mutation; it refuses completion while the last dispatched input has an effect that is not confirmed or partial, or carries an error, until an observation yields a receipt; delivery does not enter that rule. A durable native session blocks all mutation in its authority domain, across a crash, until a qualified reconciliation producer clears it. A durable browser session does the same and additionally never settles a sent action, because neither an acknowledgement nor a changed DOM establishes completion. The effector's escalation advice is carried for diagnosis only, never offered as a next step.
when_to_use: Any surface where a route can report success without acting or can act late.
when_not_to_use: As a way to make progress unattended on surfaces whose first route often no-ops: this rule hands those cases to the caller. A later extension for absolute setters, whose mechanism yields the same state whether or not an earlier application lands, needs its own test.
tradeoffs: Stops more often than any reference chain. A durable browser session stops at the first sent action, so it serves one action that must not be sent twice; durable multi-step browser work needs a completion reader bound to evidence independent of the page. An ordinary session keeps no record of an action interrupted before its result is saved, so a crash mid-action is invisible there unless the pending record is written before dispatch. Wording a goal as a target state does not make its mechanism repeat-safe: a second click on a toggle flips it.
counterexample: The reference's right-click chain continues after unverified delivery, safe only because each step re-checks for an open menu. Its no-effect reading for selection sits inside a short settle window.

transfer.target: Footwork 0aa1373 (branch codex/suno-end-to-end-20261110); source inspected, runtime not exercised
transfer.application: State the browser lane's outcomes under the three existing custody rules before widening it, weakening none, and carry the pinned driver's Confirmed and Unverifiable effect through browser_driver._effect for the default page-click route (the trusted click returns no effect readback). Add one thing to the ordinary rule: save the pending record before dispatch. Not implemented.
transfer.compatibility_checks: session_operations.py:338-349 (native durable rule); browser_authority.py:1-7, 111-124, 212-215 (every acknowledged browser send is unverifiable and a confirmed or partial effect is refused); session.py:2838-2872 (done refused over unsettled pending input, keyed on effect and error), 1084-1089 (the next observation with a receipt clears it), 2407-2420 against 2538-2625 (only the durable path writes a record before dispatch); browser_driver.py:359 (a browser effect defaults to dispatched); owned-cdp.md:39-63; durable-native-operator.md:63 (no general reconciliation producer). The pinned driver advises retry_with_page_action for a page click whose target did not change.
transfer.next_test: Five cases: a click-toggle whose effect lands after the bound, a lost reply, an acknowledged action with unreadable effect, a process death between input and saved result, and a page click the driver reads back as Confirmed. Exactly one dispatch in each. Durable browser: all five stay unknown and block the next mutation; observation does not clear them. Ordinary: the first three refuse completion until re-observed; the Confirmed case is not held; the process-death case is run before and after the pre-dispatch save, predicting completion accepted before and refused after.

validation.result: Reference source and test definitions read; no reference test run; Footwork runtime not exercised. Revised after council rounds 1 to 5 (rounds 3 to 5 partial).

novelty.difference: That card concerns keeping a bound target; this one concerns choosing the next action channel without a second dispatch.
novelty.decision: new version; v5 held completion on unknown delivery regardless of effect, which contradicts the ordinary gate, and assumed an ordinary session retains a record across a crash mid-action
